Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Staged sunset plan — termination/auto-renew redlines & coordination with Greenfield Health

Hi Claire / Procurement team,

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. Attached is our proposed MSA + Order Form draft with two tracks for term/renewal: (A) standard auto-renew with 60-day opt-out (our default) and (B) manual renewal / no auto-renew (customer opt-in) if you need an explicit non-auto-renew commitment for procurement/audit reasons.

Separately I included a short staged-sunset playbook (sunset-runbook.xlsx) that maps operations/hand-off tasks for termination-for-convenience (TFC) scenarios. Key asks from our side:
- Confirmation whether Greenfield needs a 90-day notice window instead of 60 days.
- Any mandatory data-handback or escrow requirements you must include in the MSA (audit logs, full exports, retention terms).
- If you have required language for termination fees or transition credits.

We’re happy to walk through redlines with your legal team — if you prefer, we can propose a middle path on notice (e.g., 75 days) plus a limited termination fee to preserve runway for committed capacity.

Attachments: GFH_MSA_Redlines_20261108.docx; GFH_OrderForm_Draft_20261108.pdf; sunset-runbook.xlsx

Next step: would you like a 30-min legal + ops sync on Tuesday to go through redlines?

Best,
Avery Johnson

From: Claire Benson <legal@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Procurement <procure@greenfieldhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Staged sunset plan — termination/auto-renew redlines & coordination with Greenfield Health

Avery —

Thanks for the draft. A couple of immediate notes from our side and the redlines I’m attaching: GFH_MSA_Redlines_20261108_GFH.docx (summary below).

1) Notice window: Greenfield requires 90 days for termination-for-convenience to ensure patient-facing migrations are safe. 60 days is not sufficient for critical services.
2) Auto-renew: our procurement group prefers no automatic renewals for multi-year commitments; we can consider auto-renew but only with a mandatory 90-day explicit renewal notice to customer and a manual opt-in option.
3) Data retention & audit: we must have 12 months of audit logs retained post-termination and a documented export procedure with 10 business days notice for an initial export plus a final archive delivery.
4) Transition credits: if Redwood insists on a shorter notice window, we will require a prorated termination credit (equivalent to 2 months of committed spend) to cover migration costs.

We’re open to a compromise but will need that documented. Please review my attached redlines and let me know when your legal & ops are available for a walkthrough.

Claire Benson
Senior Counsel, Greenfield Health
legal@greenfieldhealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-08T13:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Staged sunset plan — termination/auto-renew redlines & coordination with Greenfield Health

Avery —

Thanks for the forward and Claire’s notes. High-level legal position and a draft compromise below (I’ll attach a short redline in follow-up):

- Notice window: propose a compromise at 75 days for TFC. We can accept 90 days only for multi-region patient-impacting services (not for low-impact pilot environments) — we’ll need to carve those into the Order Form.
- Auto-renew: accept a default auto-renew but add an Order Form toggle so Greenfield can opt-out on a per-product basis. If they opt-in to no-auto-renew, require procurement signoff and allow only annual renewals (no mid-year changes).
- Data & exports: agree to a documented export procedure. Ops can commit to a staged export: initial data export within 10 business days after notice and final archive delivery within 45 calendar days. Require a secure transfer method and confirmation of receipt.
- Termination credits: push back on open-ended 2-month credit. Recommend a capped transition fee: either (A) one month of committed spend OR (B) a graduated credit scale tied to notice window: 0% credit for >=75 days, prorated up to 50% of one month for 60 days.

Action items for sales/ops: Ben, can you confirm whether the 45-day final archive is feasible and whether there are additional professional services hours we should price into the Order Form for a short-notice exit? Marissa, if we concede to a one-month credit, are you comfortable with the commercial impact?

I’ll produce a redline with the 75-day language and the graduated credit table for our reply to Claire.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Staged sunset plan — termination/auto-renew redlines & coordination with Greenfield Health

Karthik / team —

Ops can support the staged export / archive timeline with the following clarifications:
- Initial export: we can produce primary exports within 10 business days if Greenfield provides a list of requested datasets and an S3 bucket + access or similar transfer target.
- Final archive: 45 calendar days is feasible for standard datasets. For large-scale imaging or archived records we’ll need to scope separately — propose a PS (professional services) add-on for >5TB or complex exports.
- Cutover/hand-off: we’ll require a 10-business-day handover window where both teams run verification checks; we recommend including a final 30-day runbook period where Redwood provides limited operational support (incidents triaged only) to smooth the transition.

I attached the sunset-runbook.xlsx with the task list and estimated effort. If we agree to 75 days and the graduated credit approach Karthik suggested, ops impact is manageable. If Greenfield insists on 90 days across the board, we’ll accept but should request a longer notification for removing dedicated capacity (45 days prior to termination to free GPUs).

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: sunset-runbook.xlsx
